claims.statement: Manual refresh uses a transaction-scoped try advisory lock keyed by pgt_id plus a catalog FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED row lock, then reloads metadata to avoid replaying a stale frontier and to coordinate with scheduled refresh.
Manual refresh rejects replicas, CDC hold-mode consumption, EXTERNAL orchestration, and suspended/error tables before executing refresh work.
Refresh definition-derived SQL runs under the stored stream owner, while privileged CDC staging copies immutable per-source windows into temporary relations before changing execution identity.
Differential CDC staging uses the per-dependency interval (previous_lsn, new_lsn], with stream-table sources resolved from pgt_<id> frontier entries and optionally same-pass bypass tables.

Manual differential refresh without a supplied bound captures a WAL candidate before probing concurrent writers, requires READ COMMITTED for that proof, holds advancement at 0/0 when relevant writers exist, and merges the new frontier with the old to prevent backward progress.

Manual FULL locks sources and snapshots bounded upstream stream-table positions before TRUNCATE/INSERT, then records those positions with its baseline frontier rather than reading positions after replacement.

Scheduled protected FULL baselines use uncapped upstream buffer MAX(lsn) because locked upstream contents can include same-tick changes above the tick bound; differential windows remain capped, and differential-to-FULL fallback rereads upstream positions as a FULL baseline.

Basic refresh action selection prioritizes reinitialization over no-data, then configured mode; manual dispatch has separate TopK handling, manually rebuilds IMMEDIATE tables with FULL, and falls back to FULL when a differential frontier is missing or empty.

No-row differential refreshes can advance frontiers while preserving data_timestamp, avoiding false downstream changed-data signals; shared finalization distinguishes changed-data and no-data metadata updates.

Current incremental admission marks INTERSECT and EXCEPT as FullOnly rather than promising execution through available set-operation helpers; stored incremental-mode validation enforces admission, while FULL normalizes legacy dual-count storage.
Runtime differential guards revalidate row identity, buffers, and owner-visible RLS; shared RLS detection can execute FULL, while manual incremental prevalidation may reject RLS before execution.

Mutable CASE/IN-list aggregate drift, unsafe correlated aggregate rewrite, uncertain CASE/subquery classification, join limits, and configured delta fraction can reject differential execution through QueryTooComplex, which manual and scheduled callers handle with FULL rather than retrying every error as FULL.
A detected function-body hash change marks a table for reinitialization and returns zero differential work for that cycle.

Adaptive differential execution can choose FULL for forced/configured FULL, change ratio, buffer limit, historical cost, or aggregate saturation; refresh_strategy=differential bypasses ratio/cost/saturation heuristics but does not disable buffer safety or admission checks.
Per-leaf differential fallback changes selected snapshot leaves from NOT EXISTS to EXCEPT ALL rather than necessarily rebuilding the entire stream table with FULL.
TopK refresh recomputes and merges the ordered limited result instead of using the ordinary differential executor, with manual mode-independent dispatch and scheduled TopKRecompute reporting.

Production window plans retain partition recomputation with state-backed runtime candidates test-enabled; manual differential consumption of scoped TopK or window-strategy upstreams requires FULL, but dependency count alone is not a fallback criterion.

Differential apply routing depends on correctness and compatibility constraints: downstream consumers force explicit DML, while PH-D1, join conflict handling, distributed/partitioned targets, aggregate fast paths, and vectorized aggregate producer admission prevent treating DIFFERENTIAL as one MERGE algorithm.
The PH-D1 reconciliation layer compares result multisets against reconstructed full-query output and corrects surplus, stale, and missing rows, rather than merely deleting orphan identities.

Pipeline admission keeps small proven non-amplifying deltas direct, pipelines large or potentially amplifying ordinary deltas, and preserves compatibility exclusions; actual routing also excludes DELETE+INSERT and algebraic aggregate paths.

Portal batches stay in the caller's outer transaction and finalize frontier/history once; each fetch applies at most min(256,batch_size) tuples through a temporary relation, with oversize-byte accounting rather than a strict byte cap, and does not commit progressive target publication or release outer locks.

FULL downstream publication compares pre/post snapshots, while differential explicit DML publishes effective affected-row changes; changed values produce D/I pairs and duplicate identities are paired by occurrence to preserve multiplicity.

finalize_success requires proven downstream capture completion and updates frontier, changed/no-data metadata, completed history, typed reasons, effective mode, output-delta capture, and attached outbox in the existing transaction, propagating required durable write failures.

FULL/REINITIALIZE finalization without a typed reason fails; history distinguishes requested action, effective action, strategy, actual row counts, and full-fallback status instead of deriving execution from configured mode alone.

Stream-table buffer cleanup retains data for uninitialized consumers and otherwise deletes I/D rows only through the minimum downstream frontier; graph refresh defers member cleanup until all members have executed at the shared bound.

IMMEDIATE maintenance uses statement triggers and transition-table delta execution within the source writer transaction, with target-relation-OID advisory locks: complex shapes block exclusively, while simple scan/filter/project chains use a try-lock route allowing non-conflicting row concurrency.

IMMEDIATE TRUNCATE rebuilds target and auxiliary aggregate columns and captures a FULL pre/post diff for deferred children; FULL replacement preserves IVM triggers while selectively suppressing application triggers.

An IMMEDIATE closure refreshes only its scheduled root, relying on synchronous descendant triggers in the same READ COMMITTED transaction; deferred consumers instead use durable captured changes, and the manual path repairs a missing IMMEDIATE upstream buffer with creation plus a FULL baseline.

The ordinary scheduler wrapper rolls back panics/PG errors and AtomicityTestFailure in a refresh subtransaction and can record failure in the parent, but releases that subtransaction for other returned outcomes, including retryable/permanent outcomes returned by some finalization errors; atomicity failpoint tests do not prove rollback for every structured failure path.

Refresh atomicity tests exercise input/apply/finalize barriers, manual and scheduled injected failure recovery, caller/savepoint rollback, competing callers, next-batch concurrent writer preservation, auxiliary-state rollback, and negative controls for early progress and partial delta finalization.

Concurrency and equivalence coverage includes IMMEDIATE concurrent DML, mixed FULL/DIFFERENTIAL DAGs and mode changes, snapshot/diamond convergence across repeated rounds, and IMMEDIATE replacement/TRUNCATE/rollback integration; these are workload-specific evidence rather than universal isolation or optimized-route proofs.
